title: Self-Adjointness of Conditional Expectation
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces, with strictly positive coordinate weights summing to $1$, and let $S$ be a subset of the coordinate indices. For any real-valued functions $f,g$ on the product outcome space, their product expectation satisfies $\mathbb E_P[fE_Sg]=\mathbb E_P[(E_Sf)g]$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space
All coordinate weights are strictly positive and sum to $1$
$S$ is a subset of the coordinate indices
$f,g$ are real-valued on the product outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $S\subseteq[n]$, and $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. For conditional expectation $E_S$ onto $S$, $\mathbb E_P[fE_Sg]=\mathbb E_P[(E_Sf)g]$.
